name: Maricopa County Treasurer
notes: Researched from public treasurer.maricopa.gov pages only. Moved from the paymentus family to property-tax: the Treasurer's own site is a parcel-based tax office (I Want To > Pay My Property Taxes), with Paymentus only as the card processor. Card/digital wallet payments cost 2.25% (credit and PayPal/Venmo/Apple Pay/Google Pay) or 1.80% (debit), no minimum, one card per transaction, up to $2,000,000; the engine charges one card rate, so 2.25% is used and the debit rate is stated in help. E-check fee is not stated on the pages read (bank fee left at default). Paperless is through eNoticesOnline with the authorization code on the bill. No automatic payment program is listed. Review 2026-10-09: the Payment Options page points to the website e-check as the way to pay without an additional fee, so bankCents is 0. Review 2 (2026-10-09): the My MCTO sign-in page now loads publicly (User Name field backed by an email id, Password, Forgot Password?, Create Account), so auth is observed_public; the FAQ gives the second-half dates (March 1 / May 1) and 16% yearly interest (in help, not a one-time fee); no phone payment and no installment agreement are listed, so pay_by_phone and payment_arrangement are unsupported (inferred); main line (602) 506-8511 set as contact.

guest_pay.note: Pay by parcel without an account: card or digital wallet through Paymentus, or e-check through the website.

paperless.note: Enroll in eNotices on eNoticesOnline with the authorization code printed on your tax bill.

autopay.note: No automatic payment program is offered. Pay each half online, through your bank's bill pay, at a bank branch, by mail or in person.

pay_by_mail.note: Mail a check or money order with the payment coupon to Maricopa County Treasurer, PO Box 52133, Phoenix, AZ 85072-2133; it must be postmarked by the due date.

pay_by_phone.note: Payment Options lists no phone payment. Pay online by e-check (no fee) or card, through your bank bill pay, at an Arizona Chase branch, by mail or at 301 W. Jefferson St.

payment_arrangement.note: No installment agreement is offered online. Taxes are paid in two halves or in full by December 31; unpaid taxes accrue 16% yearly interest and can go to the February tax lien sale. Call (602) 506-8511 with questions.

help.title: Payment options
paragraphs: Card and digital payments are processed by Paymentus. Credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express) and PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay and Google Pay cost 2.25%; debit cards cost 1.80%. There is no minimum fee, the Treasurer keeps none of it, only one card may be used per transaction, and a payment can be up to $2,000,000.

To avoid a fee, pay by e-check on the Treasurer's website. Other options are an e-check through your own bank's bill pay (ask your bank; it avoids a fee), payment at a bank branch, by mail, or in person at 301 W. Jefferson St., Suite 100, Phoenix. Allow 1 to 3 business days for a payment to post.

help.title: Key property tax dates
paragraphs: Tax bills are issued each September and can be paid in two halves or in one full payment. The first half is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1 (November 2 in 2026). The second half is due March 1 of the following year and becomes delinquent after 5 p.m. on May 1.

If you miss the first-half date, you can still pay the full year by December 31 without interest when the bill is over $100. Full-year bills of $100 or less become delinquent after 5 p.m. on December 31. When a delinquency date is a weekend or holiday, it moves to 5 p.m. on the next business day.

Delinquent taxes accrue interest of 16% per year, and parcels still unpaid at the end of December are offered at the tax lien sale the following February. Not receiving a bill does not waive interest.

help.title: Go paperless with eNotices
paragraphs: To stop paper tax bills, enroll on eNoticesOnline using the authorization code printed on your tax bill. If you cannot find your bill, email the Treasurer's Office for the code.
